title: Grafana Visualization, Golden Signal Dashboards & Alertmanager Routing
summary: Master production observability visualization and alert routing: building modular Grafana dashboards for RED/USE metrics, provisioning dashboards as code via Kubernetes ConfigMaps, configuring Alertmanager routing trees with receiver inhibition and grouping, and silencing alert storms.
learningObjectives: Design production Grafana dashboards visualizing microservice golden signals (latency percentiles, error rates, RPS).
Deploy declarative Grafana dashboards as code using Kubernetes ConfigMaps with grafana_dashboard discovery labels.
Configure Alertmanager routing trees with grouping, inhibition, and deduplication to prevent notification fatigue.

curriculumModules.title: Grafana Dashboards as Code & Golden Signal Visualizations
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: Modern production teams manage Grafana dashboards as declarative code rather than manual UI point-and-click. The Grafana sidecar operator watches for Kubernetes ConfigMaps carrying label grafana_dashboard: '1', dynamically mounting the enclosed JSON dashboard into Grafana's filesystem and hot-reloading panel layouts without server restarts.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Store all production Grafana dashboard JSON models in Git repositories and deploy via GitOps using labeled ConfigMaps to eliminate snowflake dashboards and enforce peer-reviewed visual standards.

curriculumModules.title: Alertmanager Routing Trees, Deduplication & Silencing
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: Alertmanager handles alerts emitted by Prometheus, deduplicating, grouping, and routing them to external receivers (PagerDuty, Slack, Webhooks). Routing trees evaluate alert labels (severity, team, cluster), while inhibition rules suppress lower-severity alerts (e.g. Warning) if a corresponding higher-severity alert (e.g. Critical) is already firing.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Configure group_by: ['alertname', 'cluster', 'service'] with group_wait: 30s to aggregate related alert storms into a single actionable PagerDuty incident instead of firing hundreds of individual pages.

labs.title: Provisioning Declarative Grafana Dashboards as Code
labs.scenario: Provision a Golden Signals dashboard as code: author /grafana/golden-signals-dashboard.json defining timeseries panels for RPS, Error Rate, and P99 Latency. Create and apply a ConfigMap named grafana-dashboard-golden-signals in namespace monitoring labeled grafana_dashboard=1 embedding the dashboard JSON.
labs.productionContext: Declarative dashboard provisioning ensures that observability panels are versioned in Git alongside application code, preventing drift and enabling instant recovery.
objectives: Create and apply ConfigMap grafana-dashboard-golden-signals in namespace monitoring with label grafana_dashboard: '1'.
Verify ConfigMap contains dashboard data with P99 Latency.
labs.starterManifest:
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: grafana-dashboard-golden-signals
  namespace: monitoring
  labels:
    grafana_dashboard: "1"
data:
  golden-signals-dashboard.json: |
    {
      "title": "API Golden Signals RED/USE",
      "panels": [
        {"title": "Request Rate (RPS)", "type": "timeseries"},
        {"title": "Error Rate %", "type": "timeseries"},
        {"title": "Latency P99", "type": "timeseries"}
      ]
    }

steps.title: Apply labeled ConfigMap to monitoring namespace
steps.instruction: Apply the ConfigMap manifest to namespace monitoring.

validationRules.description: ConfigMap grafana-dashboard-golden-signals exists in namespace monitoring
validationRules.name: grafana-dashboard-golden-signals
validationRules.remediation: Apply ConfigMap grafana-dashboard-golden-signals in namespace monitoring

validationRules.name: grafana-dashboard-golden-signals
validationRules.remediation: Embed Latency P99 panel in golden-signals-dashboard.json

solutionCommands:
cat << 'EOF' > /grafana/dashboard-configmap.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: grafana-dashboard-golden-signals
  namespace: monitoring
  labels:
    grafana_dashboard: "1"
data:
  golden-signals-dashboard.json: |
    {
      "title": "API Golden Signals RED/USE",
      "panels": [
        {"title": "Request Rate (RPS)", "type": "timeseries"},
        {"title": "Error Rate %", "type": "timeseries"},
        {"title": "Latency P99", "type": "timeseries"}
      ]
    }
EOF

troubleshootingGuide.problem: Dashboard ConfigMap missing or label incorrect.
troubleshootingGuide.cause: The ConfigMap lacked the grafana_dashboard: '1' label or was in the wrong namespace.
troubleshootingGuide.solution: Verify metadata.labels contains grafana_dashboard: '1' and apply to namespace monitoring.

labs.title: Configuring Alertmanager Notification Trees & Inhibition Rules
labs.scenario: Configure enterprise alert notification routing: write an Alertmanager configuration to /monitoring/alertmanager.yaml defining a routing tree grouping alerts by ['alertname', 'namespace'], with group_wait: 30s, repeat_interval: 4h, and routing critical severity to receiver pagerduty-critical. Store this configuration in Secret alertmanager-main in namespace monitoring.
labs.productionContext: Fine-tuned alert routing and grouping prevents on-call alert fatigue by ensuring only actionable, aggregated alerts notify engineers via paging channels.
objectives: Create and apply Secret alertmanager-main in namespace monitoring.
Verify repeat_interval and pagerduty-critical receiver are configured.
labs.starterManifest:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: alertmanager-main
  namespace: monitoring
data:
  alertmanager.yaml: |
    global:
      resolve_timeout: 5m
    route:
      group_by: ['alertname', 'namespace']
      group_wait: 30s
      group_interval: 5m
      repeat_interval: 4h
      receiver: pagerduty-critical
    receivers:
      - name: pagerduty-critical

steps.title: Apply Alertmanager Secret to monitoring namespace
steps.instruction: Apply the Secret manifest to namespace monitoring.

validationRules.description: Secret alertmanager-main exists in namespace monitoring
validationRules.name: alertmanager-main
validationRules.remediation: Apply Secret alertmanager-main in namespace monitoring

solutionCommands:
cat << 'EOF' > /monitoring/alertmanager.yaml
global:
  resolve_timeout: 5m
route:
  group_by: ['alertname', 'namespace']
  group_wait: 30s
  group_interval: 5m
  repeat_interval: 4h
  receiver: pagerduty-critical
receivers:
  - name: pagerduty-critical
EOF

cat << 'EOF' > /monitoring/alertmanager-secret.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: alertmanager-main
  namespace: monitoring
data:
  alertmanager.yaml: |
    global:
      resolve_timeout: 5m
    route:
      group_by: ['alertname', 'namespace']
      group_wait: 30s
      group_interval: 5m
      repeat_interval: 4h
      receiver: pagerduty-critical
    receivers:
      - name: pagerduty-critical
EOF

troubleshootingGuide.problem: Secret alertmanager-main not found or config invalid.
troubleshootingGuide.cause: Secret was not applied to monitoring namespace or key was not alertmanager.yaml.
troubleshootingGuide.solution: Apply /monitoring/alertmanager-secret.yaml with key alertmanager.yaml in namespace monitoring.

assessmentQuestions.question: How does the Grafana Operator / Sidecar dynamically discover and import dashboards in Kubernetes without requiring manual dashboard JSON uploads?
options: It executes a continuous port-scan across the default namespace.

It watches Kubernetes ConfigMaps across cluster namespaces matching a designated label selector (e.g. grafana_dashboard: '1') and automatically writes the dashboard JSON to Grafana's local provisioning folder.
It requires all developers to push dashboard JSON directly into Grafana's SQLite database via SSH.
It generates SVG screenshots from web browser cookies.
assessmentQuestions.explanation: The Grafana sidecar container uses the Kubernetes API to watch for ConfigMaps with label 'grafana_dashboard: 1', automatically mounting and provisioning them into Grafana in real time.

assessmentQuestions.question: In Alertmanager architecture, what is the role of an inhibition rule?
options: It permanently deletes any alert that was not acknowledged within 15 minutes.
It mutes a target alert if a matching source alert is already firing (e.g. suppressing hundreds of 'InstanceDown' or warning alerts when a 'ClusterNetworkDown' critical alert is already active).
It stops Prometheus from scraping pods during high CPU usage.
It routes all alerts directly to email without encryption.
assessmentQuestions.explanation: Inhibition rules prevent cascading alert noise by muting downstream or warning alerts when a high-priority root-cause alert (such as an entire node or network being down) is already firing.
